title: Good-Payment Refund Standards for Security Deposits by Tier
content:
The credit department's standards for refunding Security Deposits on good payment are set by tier: the full calendar months a deposit must be held after it was paid in full before it is reviewed, the most late payment charges, returned payments and reconnections after nonpayment the service account may show in the review window, and how the refund is paid.

## Standards

| Tier | Full calendar months after the paid-in-full date | Most late payment charges in the window | Most returned payments in the window | Most reconnections after nonpayment (reconnect fees billed) in the window | Refund paid by, unless the member asks otherwise | Smallest refund paid by check on the member's request |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Residential Standard Deposit | 12 | 2 | 0 | 0 | bill credit | $50.00 |
| Residential Credit Reestablishment Deposit | 18 | 1 | 0 | 0 | bill credit | $50.00 |
| Seasonal Residence Deposit | 12 | 2 | 0 | 0 | bill credit | $50.00 |
| Farm Service Deposit | 12 | 2 | 0 | 0 | bill credit | $50.00 |
| General Service Deposit | 24 | 2 | 0 | 0 | bill credit | $50.00 |
| Irrigation and Large Power Deposit | 24 | 1 | 0 | 0 | check | $50.00 |

## Reading the standards

- The review window is the tier's number of full calendar months ending on the review date, on the service account the deposit secures.
- An allowance of 0 means a single returned payment, or a single reconnect fee, in the window is more than the standard permits.
- A check paid at the member's request applies only to a refund of at least $50.00; the Irrigation and Large Power Deposit already pays by check.
- Hypothetical illustration: a General Service Deposit account showing two late payment charges, no returned payment and no reconnect fee in its 24-month window is within the standard; the same account with three late payment charges is not.
